source_text:
Ad Carthaginiense concilium
Καὶ ὑπέγραψαν. Ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν φυλάξοι σε ἡμῖν ἐπὶ πλείστους χρόνους,
μακαριώτατε ἀδελφέ. Ὑπέγραψαν ὁμοίως· Ἀλύπιος, Αὐγουστῖνος, Ποσείδιος
, Μαρῖνος καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ ἐπίσκοποι. Ἄρχεται τὰ πρὸς τὴν ἐν Ἀφρικῇ σύνοδον
ἀντίγραφα Κυρίλλου τοῦ τῆς Ἀλεξανδρέων ἐπισκόπου, ἐν οἷς τὰ αὐθεντικὰ τῆς ἐν
Νικαίᾳ συνόδου ἀπὸ γραϊκοῦ μεταβληθέντα διὰ Ἰννοκεντίου πρεσβυτέρου
ἀπέστειλεν· αἵτινες ἐπιστολαὶ μετὰ τῆς ἐν Νικαίᾳ συνόδου διὰ τοῦ μνημονευθέντος
Ἰννοκεντίου πρεσβυτέρου καὶ Μαρκέλλου ὑποδιακόνου τῆς ἐν Καρχηδόνι ἐκκλησίας
τῷ ἁγιωτάτῳ Βονιφατίῳ, ἐπισκόπῳ τῆς ῥωμαϊκῆς ἐκκλησίας τῇ πρὸ ἓξ καλανδῶν
pass_a_gloss: Latin print title pointing the piece toward Carthage. Closing lines of the Africans’ covering note: signatures appended, a blessing wishing their brother a long life, and a matching set of signatures from Alypius, Augustine, Possidius, Marinus, plus the remaining bishops. Editorial bridge introducing Cyril’s return letters to the African synod: through the priest Innocent he forwards the genuine Nicene records rendered out of Greek; that packet, Nicene records included, traveled by way of Innocent and the Carthaginian subdeacon Marcellus to Boniface of Rome, dispatched on the sixth day before the kalends.
pass_b_english: And they signed. May our Lord keep you for us for very many years, most blessed brother. Likewise signed Alypius, Augustine, Possidius, Marinus, and the rest of the bishops.

Here begin the replies of Cyril, bishop of the Alexandrians, to the synod in Africa, in which he sent through Innocent the presbyter the authentic acts of the council at Nicaea translated from the Greek — which letters, together with the council of Nicaea, were sent through the aforementioned presbyter Innocent and Marcellus the subdeacon of the church at Carthage to the most holy Boniface, bishop of the Roman church, on the sixth day before the kalends

choices.choice: Translated from the Greek: rare γραϊκοῦ read as the source tongue.
Open ends without a period; month and verb complete in ep-rem-early.
Kept as narrative: signatures and bridge belong to the acts, not Cyril’s pen.
